The AP condition gives \(2\log_{10}(4^{x}-2)=1+\log_{10}\left(4^{x}+\tfrac{18}{5}\right)\). Put \(t=4^{x}\):
\[(t-2)^{2}=10\left(t+\tfrac{18}{5}\right)=10t+36.\]
Thus \(t^{2}-14t-32=0\Rightarrow (t-16)(t+2)=0\Rightarrow t=16\), so \(4^{x}=16\Rightarrow x=2\).
Substituting \(x=2\), the matrix becomes
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix}.\]
Expanding along the first row: \(3(0-2)-1(0-4)+4(1-0)=-6+4+4=2.\)

On \([-3,0]\), \(x+6=x^{2}\) at \(x=-2\); for \(-3\le x\le-2\) the minimum is \(x+6\), and for \(-2\le x\le0\) it is \(x^{2}\). On \([0,1]\), \(\sqrt{x}\ge x^{2}\), so the maximum is \(\sqrt{x}\). All pieces are non-negative, so
\[A=\int_{-3}^{-2}(x+6)\,dx+\int_{-2}^{0}x^{2}\,dx+\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x}\,dx.\]
\[\int_{-3}^{-2}(x+6)\,dx=\Big[\tfrac{x^{2}}{2}+6x\Big]_{-3}^{-2}=(-10)-\left(-\tfrac{27}{2}\right)=\tfrac72,\]
\[\int_{-2}^{0}x^{2}\,dx=\tfrac{8}{3},\qquad \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x}\,dx=\tfrac23.\]
So \(A=\tfrac72+\tfrac83+\tfrac23=\tfrac72+\tfrac{10}{3}=\tfrac{41}{6}\), giving \(6A=41.\)

Take \(A,B,C\) on the three segments at distance \(R\) (the circumradius) from \(O\), so \(A=R(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha)\), etc. With circumcentre at \(O\), the orthocentre is \(H=A+B+C\). \(H\) on the \(y\)-axis forces
\[\cos\alpha+\cos\beta+\cos\gamma=0.\]
Using \(\cos3\theta=4\cos^{3}\theta-3\cos\theta\),
\[\sum\cos3\theta=4\sum\cos^{3}\theta-3\sum\cos\theta=4\sum\cos^{3}\theta.\]
Since \(\cos\alpha+\cos\beta+\cos\gamma=0\), the identity \(a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}=3abc\) (when \(a+b+c=0\)) gives \(\sum\cos^{3}\theta=3\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma\). Therefore
\[\frac{\cos3\alpha+\cos3\beta+\cos3\gamma}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma}=\frac{12\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma}=12,\]
and its square is \(144.\)

Let the first \(2n\) numbers have variance \(\sigma_1^{2}\) (mean \(6\)) and the last \(n\) have variance \(\sigma_2^{2}\) (mean \(3\)). Overall mean \(=\dfrac{2n\cdot6+n\cdot3}{3n}=5\). Combined variance \(=4\):
\[\frac{2n(\sigma_1^{2}+(6-5)^{2})+n(\sigma_2^{2}+(3-5)^{2})}{3n}=4\Rightarrow 2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}=6.\]
Adding \(1\) to the first \(2n\) and subtracting \(1\) from the last \(n\) leaves each group's variance unchanged; new means are \(7\) and \(2\), new overall mean \(=\dfrac{2n\cdot7+n\cdot2}{3n}=\dfrac{16}{3}\).
\[k=\frac{2n\left(\sigma_1^{2}+(7-\tfrac{16}{3})^{2}\right)+n\left(\sigma_2^{2}+(2-\tfrac{16}{3})^{2}\right)}{3n}=\frac{2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}+2\cdot\tfrac{25}{9}+\tfrac{100}{9}}{3}.\]
With \(2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}=6\): \(k=\dfrac{6+\tfrac{150}{9}}{3}=\dfrac{68}{9}\), so \(9k=68.\)

Since \(\vec{x}\) lies in the plane of \(\vec{a}=(2,-1,1)\) and \(\vec{b}=(1,2,-1)\), write \(\vec{x}=p\,\vec{a}+q\,\vec{b}\). Let \(\vec{c}=(3,2,-1)\).
\(\vec{x}\perp\vec{c}\): with \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=3,\ \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=8\), we get \(3p+8q=0\).
Projection on \(\vec{a}\): \(\dfrac{\vec{x}\cdot\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\dfrac{17\sqrt6}{2}\), and \(|\vec{a}|=\sqrt6\), so \(\vec{x}\cdot\vec{a}=51\). With \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{a}=6,\ \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=-1\): \(6p-q=51\).
Solving \(3p+8q=0,\ 6p-q=51\) gives \(p=8,\ q=-3\). Then
\[\vec{x}=8\vec{a}-3\vec{b}=(13,-14,11),\qquad |\vec{x}|^{2}=169+196+121=486.\]

For \(P=(x,y,z)\) the sum of squared distances from the three planes is
\[\frac{(x+y+z)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(lx-nz)^{2}}{l^{2}+n^{2}}+\frac{(x-2y+z)^{2}}{6}.\]
The locus \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=9\) means this expression equals \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\) identically.
Adding the first and third terms gives \(\tfrac12 x^{2}+y^{2}+\tfrac12 z^{2}+zx\). To reach \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\), the middle term must supply \(\tfrac12 x^{2}+\tfrac12 z^{2}-zx\):
\[\frac{l^{2}}{l^{2}+n^{2}}=\frac12\Rightarrow l^{2}=n^{2},\qquad \frac{-2ln}{l^{2}+n^{2}}=-1\Rightarrow ln=l^{2}.\]
Hence \(n=l\), so \(l-n=0.\)
